title: Granular failure attributor and termination reason index
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Implement a service-layer index and attribution pipeline that consolidates termination-reasons across traces and assigns a probabilistic failure attribution score to requests. Current observability surfaces fragment termination signals (gRPC/HTTP codes, runtime preemptions, OOMs, model-level rejects/timeouts) across spans and logs; this ticket creates a canonical index (reason_code, severity, likely_root_cause, confidence) consumed by dashboards, SLI rollups, and incident automation.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A serialized termination_reason index is produced per request id and stored in the observability OLAP (daily partition).
2) Attribution algorithm classifies requests into: timeout, overload/backpressure, model_error (generation failures, tokenizer errors), model_rejection (safety), infra_preempt, out_of_memory, client_error (4xx), server_error (5xx), unknown.
3) Each classification includes a confidence score (0-100) and evidence links (span ids, log refs).
4) Dashboards show top-10 termination reasons by service, region, and model; SLI backfills correctly for last 30 days.
5) Trace enrichment hooks can attach termination_reason tags in <=2ms extra latency on sampled traces.
6) Playbook entry created with triage steps and recommended fallback policies for high-impact reasons.
tasks:
- Define termination_reason schema and canonical codes.
- Implement tracehook enrichment to emit reason hints during request lifecycle.
- Build offline scorer that replays traces to produce confidence-scored attributions.
- Wire index into OLAP and add materialized views for dashboard queries.
- Add dashboard panels for per-model and per-route breakdowns.
- Integrate with alerting: create SLO slices and persona-aware alerts.
- Write incident playbook and run tabletop with oncall to validate workflows.
notes: Design decisions and trade-offs: 1) Sampling: we will attach enriched tags to 5% of traces by default and 100% for failed request paths to control ingest volume. 2) Confidence model: start with deterministic rule engine (span markers, gRPC/HTTP codes, kv-cache-miss signatures) and iterate to ML scorer if false-positive rate >15%. 3) Enrichment must not block request path; use fire-and-forget UDP/event queue or non-blocking append to trace context. 4) To avoid double-counting in SLI backfills, materialized view uses unique request_id and picks highest-severity reason when multiple markers present. 5) Privacy: redact PII from evidence links before storing; follow KMS policy for any sensitive payloads.
